summary: The contract contains one fixed-width scalar and returns either zero or three integers, so there is no growing collection workload and the direct constant-time formula matches the problem-level lower bound.

optimality.argument: Every implementation must inspect num and decide between two fixed-size output forms, requiring constant work; divisibility, integer division, and constructing at most three values also take constant work under the source integer model.

replacement_checks.evidence: Reading the scalar input and deciding whether any representation exists requires Omega(1) work.
One remainder test, one integer division, and construction of at most three integers establish O(1) time and O(1) space.
Regression checks the complete small range, deterministic full-width values, residue boundaries, zero, and the maximum against direct algebraic conditions.
